items.name: Inspirational / motivational
items.one_line: Optimistic and forward-looking; shows the reader what is possible and that they can get there.

sources.title: Atlassian Design System: Voice and tone
sources.supports: 'optimistic' voice trait; motivating by showing what is possible; optimism scaled to how sure the reader feels

sources.title: Jungian archetypes (Wikipedia)
sources.supports: the twelve branding archetypes (Mark and Pearson) include the Hero

sources.title: Tone-of-Voice Words (NN/g)
sources.supports: 'Passionate' and 'Upbeat' are NN/g tone words

items.note: NN/g dimensions: enthusiastic, serious-to-light, respectful. Anchor uplift in a concrete story or number, or it reads as poster-quote filler.

items.name: Irreverent / edgy
items.one_line: Pokes at conventions, authority or the category itself; deliberately not polite.

sources.title: The Four Dimensions of Tone of Voice (NN/g)
sources.supports: respectful vs irreverent is one of the four tone dimensions

sources.title: Tone-of-Voice Words (NN/g)
sources.supports: 'Irreverent', 'Edgy', 'Snarky', 'Unapologetic' and 'Coarse' are NN/g tone words

items.note: NN/g dimensions: irreverent pole, usually casual and funny. Target ideas and the category, never the reader.

items.name: Journalistic neutral
items.one_line: Reports what happened and who said what, from nobody's point of view; attribution over adjectives.

sources.title: Journalistic objectivity (Wikipedia)
sources.supports: objectivity = truthfulness, neutrality and detachment; known failure is false balance between unequal claims

items.note: NN/g dimensions (inferred, not stated by a source): serious, matter-of-fact, respectful, neutral formality. Neutral does not mean equal weight for a claim the evidence does not support. BBC impartiality guidelines were blocked to the fetcher; add them at card time if reachable.

items.name: Kid-friendly
items.one_line: Short, concrete, warm sentences a child can follow, without talking down.

sources.title: Netflix English (USA) Timed Text Style Guide
sources.supports: children's programmes get a slower reading speed (up to 17 characters per second vs 20 for adults)

sources.title: Google developer documentation style guide: voice and tone
sources.supports: avoid condescending phrasing

items.note: Children's advertising rules are a compliance matter for another worker. No scary urgency, no sarcasm (children read it literally).

items.name: Luxury / premium
items.one_line: Restrained, assured and exclusive: craft, rarity and heritage, never discounts or shouting.

sources.title: Luxury goods (Wikipedia)
sources.supports: luxury brands communicate being top of their class; personalisation, special packaging and limited supply create exclusivity

items.note: Restraint (fewer adjectives, no exclamation marks, no 'cheap/offer') is common practice, not a sourced rule here; a luxury brand-voice source was not found within the search budget. Overlaps regal/heritage and minimalist.

items.name: Minimalist / understated
items.one_line: Fewest words, plain claims, white space; lets the product or fact speak.

sources.title: Microsoft Style Guide: brand voice
sources.supports: 'crisp and clear': bigger ideas, fewer words; prune every excess word; short sentences and fragments

sources.title: The Four Dimensions of Tone of Voice (NN/g)
sources.supports: matter-of-fact is the opposite pole to enthusiastic

items.note: NN/g dimensions: matter-of-fact, serious-to-dry, casual or formal. Understatement only works when the claim underneath is strong.

items.name: Nostalgic
items.one_line: Evokes a shared past (childhood, a decade, old India) to create warmth and belonging.

sources.title: Tone-of-Voice Words (NN/g)
sources.supports: 'Nostalgic' is one of NN/g's 37 tone words

items.note: Works on specific sensory details of a period, not generic 'good old days'.

items.name: Playful / witty
items.one_line: Light, clever and fun; wordplay and surprise without losing the message.

sources.title: Tone-of-Voice Samples (NN/g)
sources.supports: playful samples sit at funny + casual + irreverent + enthusiastic on the four dimensions

sources.title: The Impact of Tone of Voice on Users' Brand Perception (NN/g)
sources.supports: humorous copy hurt credibility in serious industries (study participants said friendliness took away credibility)

sources.title: Mailchimp Content Style Guide: Voice and tone
sources.supports: humour should come naturally; do not force jokes, keep a straight face when unsure; clarity beats entertainment

items.note: NN/g dimensions: funny, casual, irreverent-leaning, enthusiastic. Wrong for health, money-loss, grief or error states.

items.name: Rebellious challenger brand
items.one_line: Names the category leader or the status quo as the enemy and positions the brand as the break-out.

sources.title: Jungian archetypes (Wikipedia)
sources.supports: the Outlaw is one of the twelve branding archetypes (Mark and Pearson, The Hero and the Outlaw)

sources.title: The Four Dimensions of Tone of Voice (NN/g)
sources.supports: respectful vs irreverent dimension

items.note: NN/g dimensions: irreverent, casual, enthusiastic. Comparative claims about named competitors are a compliance matter (another worker).

items.name: Regal / heritage
items.one_line: Stately, legacy-proud voice of an old house, a royal craft or a long tradition.

sources.title: Jungian archetypes (Wikipedia)
sources.supports: the Ruler is one of the twelve branding archetypes (Mark and Pearson, The Hero and the Outlaw)

sources.title: Tone-of-Voice Words (NN/g)
sources.supports: 'Conservative' and 'Nostalgic' are NN/g tone words

items.note: NN/g dimensions: formal, serious, respectful, matter-of-fact. Back the legacy with real dates and names; invented heritage is a false claim.

items.name: Romantic
items.one_line: Tender, intimate, longing voice for love, weddings, gifting and shayari-style captions.

sources.title: Tone-of-Voice Words (NN/g)
sources.supports: 'Romantic' is one of NN/g's 37 tone words

items.note: In Hindi this register leans on Urdu vocabulary (see lang:urdu_influenced_hindi).

items.name: Sarcastic
items.one_line: Says the opposite of what it means to mock; cutting rather than gentle.

sources.title: Sarcasm (Wikipedia)
sources.supports: sarcasm is caustic, mocking use of words; it travels badly in text without vocal cues (RFC 1855 warning)

sources.title: Tone-of-Voice Words (NN/g)
sources.supports: 'Sarcastic' and 'Snarky' are NN/g tone words

items.note: NN/g dimensions: irreverent, funny. In text it needs context or markers or readers take it literally; risky in translation and captions.

items.name: Satirical (vyangya)
items.one_line: Exposes hypocrisy and folly through irony, exaggeration and mock-praise; the Hindi tradition is vyangya.

sources.title: Satire (Wikipedia)
sources.supports: satire ridicules vices and follies to criticise; Horatian (gentle) vs Juvenalian (scathing) distinction

sources.title: Harishankar Parsai (Wikipedia)
sources.supports: Parsai is the reference writer of Hindi vyangya: plain prose aimed at hypocrisy, corruption and pretence

items.note: Decide Horatian vs Juvenalian before writing. Satire needs a real target and a recognisable truth; political satire overlaps law/compliance (another worker's scope).

items.name: Storyteller / narrative
items.one_line: Carries the message inside a story: a character, a moment, a turn, a point of view.

sources.title: Storytelling (Wikipedia)
sources.supports: storytelling is increasingly used in advertising to build loyalty; core elements are plot, characters and narrative point of view

items.note: A voice, not a framework: tense, person and scene detail carry it. Story structures belong to the framework kind.

items.name: Technical / precise
items.one_line: Exact, unambiguous and consistent terminology; every sentence can be acted on.

sources.title: Google developer documentation style guide: voice and tone
sources.supports: knowledgeable-friend tone; avoid slang, jargon without need, figurative language, exclamation marks and over-politeness ('please' in steps)

items.note: NN/g dimensions: serious, matter-of-fact, respectful; casual-to-neutral formality. Simple consistent terms also help non-native readers and translation.

items.name: Tough-love coach
items.one_line: Frank, demanding and on the reader's side: names the excuse, then gives the next step.

sources.title: Tone-of-Voice Words (NN/g)
sources.supports: 'Frank' and 'Unapologetic' are NN/g tone words

items.note: NN/g dimensions: serious, casual, mildly irreverent, enthusiastic. Harsh on the behaviour, never on the person; always end with an action. Only the tone words are sourced; the coaching pattern is practice.

items.name: Urgent
items.one_line: Direct, serious and action-first when time really matters: what to do, by when, why.

sources.title: NHS digital service manual: Voice and tone
sources.supports: for serious matters such as emergencies the NHS uses direct, serious and reassuring language

items.note: Real urgency only (deadline, safety, last date). Fake scarcity and countdown pressure are a compliance matter (another worker's kind); keep exclamation marks and caps out.
